record_type_quote: A new sample of 32 healthy right-handed participants underwent behavioral motor tasks and TMS-EEG recording, in which left and right M1 were stimulated both during bimanual tasks and during an iSP paradigm.

targets.authors: Bortoletto M., Bonzano L., Zazio A., Ferrari C., Pedullà L., Gasparotti R., et al.
targets.title: Asymmetric transcallosal conduction delay leads to finer bimanual coordination.
targets.evidence_quote: In our recent study (Bortoletto et al., 2021 ), we combined TMS-EEG with diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), which provides microstructural information on callosal integrity, and with the ipsilateral silent period (iSP), a well-known peripheral measure of interhemispheric inhibition obtained from TMS and electromyography (Meyer et al., 1995 ).
targets.outcome_quote: Results show a replication of our previous findings on the positive relationship between M1-P15 amplitude and the iSP normalized area. Differently, the relationship between M1-P15 latency and bimanual coordination was not confirmed.
targets.outcome_reasoning: One explicitly replicated relationship and one explicitly unconfirmed relationship from the same original paper. The general validation conclusion concerns the marker rather than an overall verdict covering both comparisons.

targets.authors: Giovannelli F., Borgheresi A., Balestrieri F., Zaccara G., Viggiano M. P., Cincotta M., et al.
targets.title: Modulation of interhemispheric inhibition by volitional motor activity: an ipsilateral silent period study.
targets.evidence_quote: In fact, during the iSP paradigm we manipulated the activity of the contralateral hand, expecting to induce a stronger interhemispheric inhibition in the Contracted compared to the Relaxed condition (Giovannelli et al., 2009 ), which we did not observe.
targets.outcome_quote: In fact, during the iSP paradigm we manipulated the activity of the contralateral hand, expecting to induce a stronger interhemispheric inhibition in the Contracted compared to the Relaxed condition (Giovannelli et al., 2009 ), which we did not observe. The null result on iSP modulation was surprising, considering the consistent effects reported previously throughout several manipulations of contralateral hand activity (Giovannelli et al., 2009 ).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The predicted published contraction effect was directly tested but not observed; the authors do not give a verdict that the attempt as a whole was incapable of adjudication.
